issues: The source does not identify the first-person narrator as Nephi; labeling the character as Nephi relies on the scene’s supplied note, not these verses. The seraphim are described as standing above “it,” whose referent is unspecified. The scene correctly flags this uncertainty and does not resolve it visually. The stated elevated-throne inference is supported by “high and lifted up.”
The verse identifies the speaker only as “I”; identifying him as Nephi is not established by the supplied verses. The quotation itself is exact.
Whether the King was seen earlier or at the time of speech is unspecified; avoid depicting the reported sight as a present event.

The coal is explicitly said to have been taken from the altar with tongs, but depicting that earlier act as part of this scene would combine separate times; the scene description should show only the seraph arriving with the coal and then laying it on the mouth.
Nephi is named as present, but the verses identify only a first-person narrator; his identity as Nephi is not established by these supplied verses.

The verses leave the speaker and addressee unidentified; the scene appropriately avoids naming them. The preceding scene identifies Nephi and the Lord, but this passage does not explicitly establish that either is the speaker or addressee.
The summary is a paraphrase of the passage, not dialogue; the dialogue and narration use exact source excerpts.

The reply is introduced as “he said,” but the text does not explicitly identify the speaker as the Lord; “The Lord” as speaker and respondent is a reasonable inference from Nephi’s address, not an explicit fact.

The narration “Then said I:” and “And he said:” is an exact excerpt from verse 11, but the summary’s “Nephi asks” depends on identifying the first-person narrator as Nephi, which is not established in the supplied verses themselves.
The dialogue quotes are contiguous and exact; the reply reports future desolation and must not be staged as present action, as the scene’s prohibition correctly notes.
